value: US EPA Office of Air and Radiation (2012). Available and Emerging Technologies for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions from the Iron and Steel Industry. Prepared by the Sector Policies and Programs Division, Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Research Triangle Park, NC, September 2012.

Loaded (main file): whole technologies with their own energy use or cost - DC arc furnace (electricity range, incremental capex over AC per t capacity, electrode flow), strip caster (fuel and electricity), thin-slab casting capex, continuous annealing line (plant cost and capacity), ladle preheating gas use, rolling-mill drive electricity, CHP capex range, PSH furnace demo plant and Essar DRI/EAF plant (capex and capacity), U.S. average energy intensities (integrated mill, EAF mill, coke), and per-t CO2 factors for sinter, BOF, EAF, by-product and heat-recovery coke ovens; BF mass flows in _flows.csv. Not loaded: the energy-efficiency measure catalogue (Tables 1-2, C-1, C-2 and Sect. VII text: savings, retrofit capital per t product, payback, applicability codes) goes to _measures.csv; plant lists, sector emission totals, gas compositions and other context go to _other-values.csv. Most numbers are reprinted from Worrell 1999/2009/2010, DOE, IPCC or AP-42 and are flagged in notes; the report's own results are the EPA AP-42 coke factors and the Appendix D emission estimates.

(1) Blanket price-year statement (all costs in 2008 dollars, Worrell 1994 costs x1.56 CEPCI) is applied also to non-Worrell figures (e.g. $225 million annealing line, CHP $900-2,500/kW); Appendix A costs (PSH, Essar) carry no year. (2) Cost basis (equipment/installed/total) never stated; Table C costs are 'retrofit capital costs' per tonne of product without saying whether per tonne of annual capacity. (3) Unit conversion errors: 181 kWh/ton printed as 0.072 GJ/tonne (should be ~0.72); coke 3.4 MMBtu/ton printed as 2.9 GJ/tonne (should be ~3.95); oxy-fuel savings 18-36 kWh/ton printed as 0.72-0.14 GJ/tonne; oxy-fuel 88-155 kWh/ft3 printed as 11-20 GJ/m3. (4) BOF gas recovery: text gives ~$20/tonne capital, Table C-1 gives $34.4/tonne. (5) Thin slab casting: Table C-1 and C-2 give different CO2 and fuel savings (728.8 vs 265.3 kg; 3.5 vs 3.2 GJ) for the same measure; text gives 4.9 GJ/tonne. (6) Table C-1 'CHP' row lists fuel 0.03 GJ and electricity 0.35 GJ savings without basis. (7) Section A.1 says four ULCOS concepts but lists three. (8) Heating-value basis is never stated.
